preamble: Spirantization of the aspirated alveolar affricate [tsʰ] to the sibilant [s]. Wikipedia's Hainanese article says that the etymological aspirated stops of Hainanese have spirantized in the more innovative varieties and gives the affricate's outcome as [ɕ] (*pʰ > [ɸ], *tʰ > [h], *tsʰ > [ɕ], *kʰ > [h~x]); its consonant table marks /tsʰ/ as present in the Banqiao dialect. For Haikou the sources print [s]: the Haikou initials that Wikipedia lists after Chen (1996) include s but neither ɕ nor any aspirated stop or affricate, and Wiktionary's dialect readings give Haikou [s] for words with Norman's Proto-Min initial *tsh, which Xiamen, Fuzhou, Jian'ou and Shaowu keep as [tsʰ]: 秋 'autumn' /siu²³/, 草 'grass' /sau²¹³/. The same readings give Haikou s- for 七 'seven' /sit̚⁵/, 千 'thousand' /sin²³/ and 清 'clear' /seŋ²³/.

examples.note: Xiamen /t͡sʰiu⁵⁵/, Fuzhou /t͡sʰieu⁴⁴/ and Jian'ou /t͡sʰiu⁵⁴/ keep the affricate.
